title: E2E Test Plan (Draft) — Model Release Notes + Changelog (Metadata v1)
content:
Owner: Leila
Last pass goal: define E2E coverage for (1) metadata edits + schema validation, (2) event emission + changelog generator, (3) Console views (release notes feed + per-model history), (4) docs-site build consumption, (5) audit logging + RBAC/redaction.

This is a draft QA plan. We should treat it as an evolving checklist that tracks what we can automate vs what needs manual validation for the first GA. Any scenario marked “BLOCKER” should be automated before GA unless we explicitly waive.

---

1) Scope & quality bar

In scope (MVP):
- Model metadata schema v1 validation + required fields (ENG-9821, ENG-9826)
- Model registry migration/backfill health checks (ENG-9822)
- Control plane event emission for metadata updates + version promotion + deprecation actions (pr-18435)
- Changelog generator ingestion + templating + category mapping + public/internal filtering (pr-18441)
- Console backend + UI consumption of release notes feed and per-model change history w/ pagination/filters (pr-18447, ENG-9824)
- RBAC and “public vs internal” separation for Console and generated artifacts (ENG-9825, pr-18463)
- Audit log events emitted for create/update/promote/deprecate and available via internal query for Support/Compliance (ENG-9828, pr-18458)
- Docs build consumes generated artifacts to publish versioned release note pages (redwood-docs pr-9312)
- Private export packaging (high-level validation only in MVP; deeper offline tests can follow) (ENG-9829)

Out of scope:
- Full notification subscriptions (email/webhook) beyond internal plumbing
- Full historical backfill of release notes (only limited backfill)

Quality bar:
- No internal-only text should be visible to non-admin roles in Console OR in public docs artifacts (BLOCKER).
- Metadata changes must be traceable end-to-end: registry record -> event -> changelog entry -> Console display -> docs pages (with stable ids) (BLOCKER).
- Schema validation failures must fail CI with actionable errors; release note preview artifact must be generated on metadata diffs (BLOCKER).
- Audit events must be emitted for every change type + contain minimum fields required by security/compliance (BLOCKER for enterprise beta).

---

2) Environments, test data, and accounts

Environments:
- dev: local + ephemeral stacks (fast iteration; not authoritative)
- staging: primary E2E environment for pipeline correctness (authoritative)
- prod: limited smoke checks only; NO redaction experiments (to avoid accidental leak)

Test users / roles (Console):
- role_admin: Redwood employee admin (full access incl internal fields)
- role_support: internal support role (audit/changelog admin surfaces; confirm internal access but no edit)
- role_customer_owner: standard customer account owner (can view public release notes and model history)
- role_customer_viewer: read-only customer role (should see same public notes, no internal)

Test accounts:
- acct_sandbox_public: standard Hosted sandbox account
- acct_enterprise_beta: enterprise-like staging tenant w/ Dedicated enabled (mimic SLA/RBAC config)
- acct_private_packaging: tenant configured for Private export tests

Test models/fixtures (must exist in staging):
- “rw.qwen2.5-72b-instruct” (or similar) — baseline text/chat model
- “rw.llama-3.1-70b-instruct” — second family for compatibility validation
- Quantization variants: fp16 + int8 (and any supported “profile” in schema)
- At least one deprecated model version (for deprecation + docs behavior)

Data hygiene:
- All test metadata notes must use synthetic wording, no customer names, no internal incident details.
- Use a dedicated “E2E TEST DO NOT SHIP” marker in internal fields to validate redaction filters.

---

3) Observability and artifacts to capture

For each E2E run, capture:
- metadata payload diff (before/after)
- CI logs for schema validation + release note preview job
- emitted events (from event bus or event log table) with correlation ids
- generator output artifact (JSON) as stored for Console/docs consumption
- Console API response payloads (admin vs customer role)
- docs build output (staging URL + rendered page snippet)
- audit log entries for the change

Key identifiers we must be able to correlate:
- model_id, model_version (semver), variant_id (quant profile), schema_version/hash
- change_event_id and/or idempotency key
- release_note_entry_id

---

4) E2E scenario matrix (high level)

P0 / BLOCKER scenarios:
A. Metadata edit (non-breaking) -> event -> changelog -> Console + docs show update (public) and internal-only notes only for admin.
B. Version promotion (canary -> GA) -> changelog entry shows rollout status (where appropriate) -> Console feed ordering and filters correct.
C. Rollback (promoted version reverted) -> changelog reflects rollback + guidance link; Console history shows rollback event.
D. Redaction enforcement: internal fields never appear for non-admin roles, across Console UI, API, docs artifacts.
E. CI gate: metadata schema validation failure blocks merge; release note preview artifact generated on valid change.
F. Audit logs: create/update/promote/deprecate/rollback produce audit events with required fields; support can query.

P1 scenarios:
G. Deprecation + timeline fields -> docs display deprecation banner; Console shows deprecation in history.
H. Multi-deployment availability differences (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) reflected correctly in release notes and filters.
I. Pagination / filtering correctness on high volume change history.
J. Generator idempotency on duplicate events / retries.

P2 scenarios:
K. Backfill migration: existing records produce consistent minimal release notes; no empty/incomplete pages.
L. Regional availability filtering (if in v1); at minimum “deployment mode” filtering.

---

5) Detailed scenarios and acceptance criteria

Scenario A (P0): Metadata edit (public-only change)
Goal: verify the basic pipeline works for a safe, non-breaking change.
Preconditions:
- staging has model version X.Y.Z live and viewable in Console
Steps:
1. Create a metadata PR in model registry updating a public field (e.g., “performance_notes.public” or “bugfix_notes.public”) with a small text change.
2. Ensure the PR includes required release-note capture fields/labels as per release eng guidance.
3. Merge PR; confirm CI passes and release note preview artifact is attached to the PR.
4. Confirm control plane emits “model_metadata_changed” event referencing model_id, version, schema hash.
5. Confirm changelog generator ingests event and produces a release note entry with category=bugfix|perf|quality (as configured).
6. Console (role_customer_owner) opens model page -> Change History shows new entry with correct timestamp, category, and summary.
7. Console (role_admin) sees same entry plus internal-only fields (if present).
8. Docs build (staging) publishes the entry to the model release notes page (no internal text).
Expected / acceptance:
- Console and docs content match the generated artifact (no drift).
- No internal-only fields appear for role_customer_owner.
- Entry includes stable id, timestamp, and links to guidance (if configured).
- Ordering: newest entry appears at top; timestamp consistent within expected delay (SLO target TBD; for staging allow <= 5 minutes).

Scenario B (P0): Version promotion event (canary -> GA)
Goal: verify promotion is treated as a distinct change type with correct language.
Preconditions:
- Two versions exist: X.Y.(Z-1) currently default; X.Y.Z is eligible for canary.
Steps:
1. Trigger a version promotion in staging (via admin tooling / control plane) from canary to GA for Hosted.
2. Verify “model_version_promoted” event emitted with from_version/to_version, rollout policy id (if present), deployment=Hosted.
3. Verify generator creates release note entry classified as “rollout” (or “release”) with appropriate template.
4. Console release notes feed shows the promotion entry in global feed and on model page.
5. Filter by deployment=Hosted: entry visible. Filter by deployment=Dedicated: not visible unless applicable.
Expected:
- Entry does NOT claim quality improvements unless metadata includes eval signals and they pass publishing rules.
- Entry language aligns with taxonomy/style guide (avoid overstating).
- If a customer pins to old version, change history still reflects promotion but should not imply their pinned config changed.

Scenario C (P0): Rollback after promotion
Goal: confirm rollback is visible, explicit, and provides supportability.
Preconditions:
- Scenario B completed; version X.Y.Z is GA default.
Steps:
1. Trigger rollback to X.Y.(Z-1) (Hosted) due to simulated regression.
2. Confirm rollback event emitted (type may be “model_version_promoted” with direction, or distinct “rollback” type—verify actual schema).
3. Generator creates release note entry category=bugfix|rollback (depending on taxonomy mapping).
4. Console model history shows rollback entry and indicates previous default restored.
5. Confirm docs page shows rollback entry and any guidance link (e.g., “How to pin model versions”).
Expected:
- Rollback entry clearly states scope (deployment mode, any regions) and impact.
- Audit log captures actor, reason, and before/after versions.

Scenario D (P0): Public vs internal separation (redaction)
Goal: prove we cannot leak internal fields through any surface (Console, API, docs).
Preconditions:
- A change event exists with BOTH public and internal note fields set.
Steps:
1. Update metadata with:
   - public summary: “Improved throughput on long-context requests.”
   - internal note: “E2E TEST DO NOT SHIP: includes kernel flag name + incident reference.”
2. Generate release note entry.
3. Validate via Console UI:
   a) role_admin sees internal note.
   b) role_support sees internal note (if policy allows) OR sees audit-only detail (confirm spec).
   c) role_customer_owner and role_customer_viewer do not see internal note.
4. Validate via Console API responses:
   - call release notes endpoint with customer token; ensure internal fields absent (not empty string, absent entirely or redacted placeholder per API contract).
5. Validate docs build artifact:
   - generated JSON feed for docs contains no internal note fields.
   - rendered HTML page contains no internal content.
6. Negative test: attempt to pass “internal” content in a field that is supposed to be public (e.g., using prohibited keywords) and ensure CI redaction checks fail if such linting exists.
Expected:
- Zero internal strings are present in customer-facing surfaces.
- Regression test coverage exists for the previous issue (ref pr-18463: “internal notes shown to non-admins”).

Scenario E (P0): CI schema validation + release note preview
Goal: validate that metadata diffs produce reviewable output and that invalid schemas block merges.
Steps (invalid schema):
1. Create PR with missing required field (e.g., version semver invalid, missing tokenizer requirement).
2. CI fails with clear error specifying missing/invalid field and link to schema docs.
Steps (valid schema):
3. Create PR with a valid change.
4. CI produces “Release Note Preview” artifact showing:
   - category
   - severity (if applicable)
   - customer-visible summary
   - affected deployment modes
   - links
Expected:
- CI gating aligns with Connor/Sahana’s checklist; reviewers can approve content before promotion.

Scenario F (P0): Audit log event emission and query
Goal: satisfy security/compliance expectation for change visibility.
Steps:
1. Perform each change type in staging:
   - create new model record
   - update metadata
   - promote version
   - deprecate version
   - rollback (if distinct)
2. Confirm audit event exists for each action with minimum fields:
   - event_type
   - actor (service + user if applicable)
   - timestamp
   - model_id, version, variant
   - environment/deployment mode
   - change_summary (safe)
   - request id / correlation id
3. Using internal admin endpoint/tooling, query audit events by model_id and time range.
4. Verify retention/forwarding hooks are present in staging (best-effort; confirm event format matches Confluence doc).
Expected:
- Audit events are emitted exactly once per logical change (idempotent in retries).
- For customer-facing release notes, we do NOT rely on audit logs; but audit logs provide investigative trail.

Scenario G (P1): Deprecation timeline + customer messaging
Steps:
1. Mark a version as deprecated with:
   - deprecation_date
   - end_of_support_date
   - recommended_replacement_version
   - public guidance link
2. Confirm generator creates deprecation entry category=deprecation.
3. Console shows deprecation badge on version; history entry includes dates.
4. Docs show deprecation section/badge.
Expected:
- Language meets style guide; avoids “breaking” unless actually breaking.

Scenario H (P1): Deployment availability mismatch
Goal: ensure we don’t mislead customers when Dedicated/Private lag Hosted.
Steps:
1. Promote version for Hosted only.
2. Confirm release note entry indicates availability “Hosted: now”, “Dedicated: pending/eligible”, “Private: next bundle” (as per schema fields).
3. In Console, filter by deployment mode.
Expected:
- Customer sees accurate availability for their deployment.

Scenario I (P1): Pagination + filtering at scale
Steps:
1. Create 50+ metadata changes across a single model (script or backfill).
2. Verify Console history endpoint pagination stable (no duplicates/missing across page boundaries).
3. Filtering by category/deployment returns consistent counts.
Expected:
- Deterministic ordering (timestamp desc, tie-breaker by entry id).

Scenario J (P1): Generator idempotency / retry behavior
Steps:
1. Replay the same event twice (or simulate generator restart and reprocessing).
2. Confirm only one changelog entry exists.
3. Simulate partial failure (ingest ok, write fails, retry).
Expected:
- Exactly-once semantics at the “entry visible” level (idempotent key works).

Scenario K (P2): Migration backfill sanity
Steps:
1. Run migration job in staging.
2. Spot check N models across families: required fields filled, defaults set.
3. Verify Console doesn’t crash on legacy records; docs doesn’t publish empty release note pages.
Expected:
- No “unknown” placeholders that violate public style.

Scenario L (P2): Regional filtering (if supported)
Steps:
1. Mark availability by region in metadata (if field exists).
2. Console filter by region returns correct subset.

---

6) Automation strategy

What we will automate (target by GA):
- API-level E2E tests in staging for scenarios A–F (P0), including RBAC redaction assertions.
- Snapshot tests for generator templates (category mapping + redaction).
- CI tests for schema validation and release note preview generation.

What may remain manual for beta:
- Docs build visual validation (HTML rendering + IA) for key scenarios (A, D, G). We can automate later with DOM assertions in the docs pipeline.
- Private packaging export validation (depends on bundle tooling maturity).

Suggested harness:
- Use Playwright for Console UI critical-path checks (login, model page, history feed), but prefer API assertions where possible.
- For event/generator, prefer black-box tests that poll generator output store for expected entry ids.

---

7) Exit criteria (proposal)

For beta (1–2 enterprise accounts):
- All P0 scenarios pass in staging with automation evidence.
- At least 1 end-to-end run including promotion + rollback + audit log query.
- No open P0 bugs related to redaction/RBAC.

For GA:
- P0 automated and running in nightly pipeline.
- P1 scenarios H–J passing or explicitly waived with documented risk.
- Support runbook validated: Support can retrieve per-model change history + audit events for a customer escalation.

---

8) Known risks / open questions

- Exact event type naming for rollback: confirm whether we emit a separate “rollback” event or reuse “version_promoted” with metadata.
- Publishing rules for eval metrics: what qualifies as “meaningful” and what’s allowed publicly (need final from Jonas/Sana + style guide alignment).
- How we represent “customer pinned” configs in release notes: should we annotate “does not affect pinned versions” automatically?
- RBAC matrix: does role_support get internal notes or only audit details? Need final policy from Security (Marcus/Naomi).
- Latency SLO for propagation (event -> generator -> Console/docs). We need a target; tests can assert within threshold.

---

9) Quick checklist (copy/paste for test runs)

Run header:
- Date:
- Env:
- Model/version:
- Actor:
- Links (PR, build, artifact URLs):

Checklist:
[ ] Schema validation passed
[ ] Release note preview artifact generated
[ ] Event emitted (id + payload captured)
[ ] Generator entry created (id + artifact captured)
[ ] Console customer view correct
[ ] Console admin view correct
[ ] Docs page updated (no internal text)
[ ] Audit event recorded and queryable

(End)
